The said patient denied a prior exposure to the smartphone screen protector glue but recalled past exposure to manicure products with acrylates once 2 years before with good tolerance to them. The patient came back on D18 after noting new 2+ reactions involving the areas where we had patch tested ACMO and HEMA (as part of the GEIDAC extended baseline series at the time) on her back. Reactions followed a crescendo pattern over the following days (3+ on D36). The patient accepted further patch tests 3 months thereafter and both substances became positive on D2 and D4. She was diagnosed as having a late reaction to HEMA and ACMO.
